problems.problem: The declared concept specifies 'fine engraved vertical rib lines inside the band only', but the rendered nude band reads as a flat, unmodulated beige stripe with no legible rib engraving at poster scale. The band is the conceptual payload (grosgrain magnified into a horizon); without visible rib density it collapses into a generic color block, and the bottle's own fluted glass becomes the only rib texture in the frame, inverting the intended dialogue.

The nameplate stacks two identical words: logo 'Chloé' (30px, y94) directly above title 'Chloé' (150px, y187). Read together they form a stuttering duplicate rather than a brand-mark/nameplate hierarchy; references resolve this by differentiating content (brand mark vs product name) or scale gap. The small logotype also sits only ~79px above the title cap, crowding the plate.

The meridian rule (decoration, 173px wide at y377) floats in a large empty blue field with ~190px of dead space between it and the band top edge, so the 'ribbon gauge line' reads as a stray dash instead of a tick on the meridian system; its nude color on blue also lacks the crisp ink authority the concept assigns to the nameplate zone.

Illumination is coherent (shadowless frontal graphic light matches the high-key packshot), but the blue field is a perfectly uniform matte with no printed-ink character; against references 3-5, whose fields carry either caustic light play, gradient depth or reflective ground, this field reads slightly pasted-behind rather than printed-with, weakening the screen-print card illusion.

changes.value: Seamless flat matte screen-printed card in medium dusty cornflower blue with faint paper-grain ink settle, one hard-edge horizontal grosgrain nude-beige band crossing at four tenths down the frame, inside the band only a dense row of fine engraved vertical rib lines like magnified ribbon weave catching slightly darker beige ink, perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, no texture gradients outside the band, no objects
